description: A Snowflake Scripting variable may be DECLAREd or LET with a PARAMETRISED type such as NUMBER(38,2) or VARCHAR(20). Previously the DECLARE / LET grammar accepted only a bare type name, so the precision, scale or length parenthesis failed to parse. The scale is not decoration: NUMBER(10,2) ROUNDS an assigned 3.14159 to 3.14, which is the cell that shows the parameters reached the type rather than merely parsing. Converted 1:1 from scripting/ScriptTypedDeclareParamsTest (now retired); the numeric readings are taken through ::VARCHAR so the rendered SCALE is visible and reads the same on every transport.

steps.sql: DECLARE profit NUMBER(38, 2) DEFAULT 0.0; BEGIN RETURN profit::VARCHAR; END;
BEGIN LET p NUMBER(38, 2) := 12.5; RETURN p::VARCHAR; END;
DECLARE amt NUMBER(10, 2); BEGIN amt := 3.14159; RETURN amt::VARCHAR; END;
DECLARE name VARCHAR(20) := 'Alice'; BEGIN RETURN name; END;
